# How do I create a Pylon API token?

Last updated: August 29, 2026

Applies to: Pylon API access

To create a Pylon API token, sign in as a user with permission to manage API tokens, then open Settings → API Tokens. If you do not see that page, ask a workspace admin to create the token or update your access.

  1. Open Settings → API Tokens.

  2. Select Create.

  3. Enter a token name, then finish creation.

  4. Copy the token immediately and store it in a secure location. Pylon only shows the full token value once.

Use the token to authenticate Pylon API requests with a Bearer header:

  * `Authorization: Bearer <token>`

If you need read-only access, a workspace admin should choose an appropriate role for the token when creating it.

# Authentication

How to authenticate with Pylon's API

The Pylon API uses Bearer authentication. This means you’ll need to pass your API token in the header of your request:

Copy
    
    `Authorization: Bearer <token>`

Generate an API token in the Pylon dashboard.

Once creating a token, you can hit the `/me` endpoint to retrieve details about your organization to confirm your token is working as expected.

Actions performed by the token will show up with name of the token.

Pylon’s API can be used to programmatically access and take action on data within Pylon.

Some common use cases for our API include:

# How do I connect to the Pylon MCP Server?

Last updated: October 29, 2026

The Pylon MCP server at https://mcp.usepylon.com provides AI tools access to your Pylon data. The endpoint uses HTTPS, so the connection is protected with TLS. It uses OAuth authentication with your Pylon account.

The application you connect to Pylon's MCP will only have access to data you would have access to in Pylon, and will read and write on behalf of you.

## Common Clients

### Claude Code
    
    `claude mcp add pylon --transport http https://mcp.usepylon.com/`

Then, in Claude Code, run the `/mcp` command and select the `pylon` MCP to authenticate.

`--transport http` selects MCP's Streamable HTTP transport and stateless request handling; it does not mean that the connection is unencrypted or uses a plaintext HTTP URL. The Pylon endpoint remains HTTPS/TLS-protected.

### Claude Desktop and Web

In "Admin Settings", add a custom connector named "Pylon" with URL `https://mcp.usepylon.com/`

Leave "OAuth Client ID" and "OAuth Client Secret" blank.

Navigate to "Settings > Connectors" and click the "Connect" button next to the Pylon MCP to authenticate.

### ChatGPT

Image: CleanShot 2026-02-19 at 20.26.36.png

In the Apps tab, search for Pylon and install our native ChatGPT app.

### Cursor

Add to your Cursor MCP settings:

`~/.cursor/mcp.json` :
    
    `{
      "mcpServers": {
        ...
        "pylon": {
          "url": "https://mcp.usepylon.com/"
        }
        ...
      }
    }`

Navigate to "Cursor Settings > Tools & MCP" and click "Connect" next to the Pylon MCP to authenticate.

Save the code as `pylon.mjs` in a project set up as in Set up your project, and run it with the scheduled sync runner: `import { syncPylon as sync } from './pylon.mjs';`. For an EU tenant, also set `PYLON_API_URL=https://api.eu.usepylon.com`.

  * History first: `node run.mjs 2025-01-01` sends every message since that date to `/trackhistorical`. Then start a backfill from the Backfill tab.
  * Then every 15 minutes: the scheduled job sends new messages to `/track`, and they are enriched automatically every day. A message that is more than an hour old when the job sees it goes to `/trackhistorical`, and needs a backfill.
  * Re-runs are safe: duplicates are removed automatically.

Each issue costs one messages call, and the messages endpoint allows 120 calls a minute shared across your organization, so a history load takes a while and can slow other Pylon integrations; the code waits whenever Pylon asks it to. MCP connectors now live on Settings > AI controls > Connectors, alongside Pylon's built-in tools, API tools, and codebase connectors.

## Authentication

Custom MCP connectors in Pylon support two authentication patterns:

  * OAuth - Pylon's MCP client connects over Streamable HTTP and implements the MCP authorization spec (2025-06-18), using PKCE (RFC 7636) and discovering OAuth endpoints via Protected Resource Metadata (RFC 9728) and Authorization Server Metadata (RFC 8414).

  * Static token methods - the connector form also supports bearer token, `API-Key`, `X-Api-Key`, and Basic authentication for MCP servers that accept those headers.

For OAuth-based MCP connections, a connector can obtain its OAuth client in one of two ways:

  * Dynamic Client Registration - if the MCP server advertises a registration endpoint per RFC 7591, Pylon registers itself automatically on the first connect, so no Client ID is required.

  * Manual Client ID - for servers that don't support dynamic registration, register an OAuth app with the provider yourself and paste the Client ID and, optionally, the Client Secret into the connector.

For people working in Claude, OAuth keeps each person acting as themselves, which is how the Claude connector signs in.

## Step 2, option C: connect Claude Code

Run this in your terminal (Claude integration page, Pylon MCP docs):

`claude mcp add pylon --transport http https://mcp.usepylon.com/`

Then run `/mcp` inside Claude Code, select pylon, and sign in. EU workspaces use `https://mcp.eu.usepylon.com` instead. `--transport http` selects MCP's Streamable HTTP transport. The connection to Pylon stays HTTPS.

Headless runs and scripts. Claude Code can't run the OAuth sign-in in a `claude -p` or Agent SDK run, so complete sign-in from an interactive session first (Claude Code MCP docs). For a worker that never signs in interactively, use a Pylon API token instead. Pylon accepts it as an `Authorization: Bearer <API_TOKEN>` header on the regional URL, and the token must belong to the same region (Pylon MCP docs). Claude Code adds headers with `--header`:

`claude mcp add --transport http pylon https://mcp.usepylon.com --header "Authorization: Bearer <API_TOKEN>"`

Only Admins can create API tokens in Pylon (roles and user management). A token with its own identity uses the role assigned to it. A token linked to a teammate or bot uses that user's current role. Either way the identity needs MCP Access, and any IP allowlist on the token also applies to MCP requests. If Claude Code has a header configured and Pylon rejects it, Claude Code reports a failed connection rather than falling back to OAuth.
